history.content:
Please solve this issue: Wrong URL generated by get_admin_url for readonly field in custom Admin Site
Description
	
When a model containing a ForeignKey field is viewed (or edited) in a custom Admin Site, and that ForeignKey field is listed in readonly_fields, the url generated for the link is /admin/... instead of /custom-admin/....
This appears to be caused by the following line in django.contrib.admin.helpers get_admin_url:
url = reverse(url_name, args=[quote(remote_obj.pk)])
Other parts of the admin use the current_app keyword parameter to identify the correct current name of the Admin Site. (See django.contrib.admin.options.ModelAdmin response_add as just one example)
I have been able to correct this specific issue by replacing the above line with:
url = reverse(
	url_name,
	args=[quote(remote_obj.pk)],
	current_app=self.model_admin.admin_site.name
)
However, I don't know if there are any side effects and I have not yet run the full suite of tests on this. Mostly looking for feedback whether I'm on the right track.

Please solve this issue: Wrong URL generated by get_admin_url for readonly field in custom Admin Site
Description
	
When a model containing a ForeignKey field is viewed (or edited) in a custom Admin Site, and that ForeignKey field is listed in readonly_fields, the url generated for the link is /admin/... instead of /custom-admin/....
This appears to be caused by the following line in django.contrib.admin.helpers get_admin_url:
url = reverse(url_name, args=[quote(remote_obj.pk)])
Other parts of the admin use the current_app keyword parameter to identify the correct current name of the Admin Site. (See django.contrib.admin.options.ModelAdmin response_add as just one example)
I have been able to correct this specific issue by replacing the above line with:
url = reverse(
	url_name,
	args=[quote(remote_obj.pk)],
	current_app=self.model_admin.admin_site.name
)
However, I don't know if there are any side effects and I have not yet run the full suite of tests on this. Mostly looking for feedback whether I'm on the right track.

Please solve this issue: Wrong URL generated by get_admin_url for readonly field in custom Admin Site
Description
	
When a model containing a ForeignKey field is viewed (or edited) in a custom Admin Site, and that ForeignKey field is listed in readonly_fields, the url generated for the link is /admin/... instead of /custom-admin/....
This appears to be caused by the following line in django.contrib.admin.helpers get_admin_url:
url = reverse(url_name, args=[quote(remote_obj.pk)])
Other parts of the admin use the current_app keyword parameter to identify the correct current name of the Admin Site. (See django.contrib.admin.options.ModelAdmin response_add as just one example)
I have been able to correct this specific issue by replacing the above line with:
url = reverse(
	url_name,
	args=[quote(remote_obj.pk)],
	current_app=self.model_admin.admin_site.name
)
However, I don't know if there are any side effects and I have not yet run the full suite of tests on this. Mostly looking for feedback whether I'm on the right track.

Please solve this issue: Wrong URL generated by get_admin_url for readonly field in custom Admin Site
Description
	
When a model containing a ForeignKey field is viewed (or edited) in a custom Admin Site, and that ForeignKey field is listed in readonly_fields, the url generated for the link is /admin/... instead of /custom-admin/....
This appears to be caused by the following line in django.contrib.admin.helpers get_admin_url:
url = reverse(url_name, args=[quote(remote_obj.pk)])
Other parts of the admin use the current_app keyword parameter to identify the correct current name of the Admin Site. (See django.contrib.admin.options.ModelAdmin response_add as just one example)
I have been able to correct this specific issue by replacing the above line with:
url = reverse(
	url_name,
	args=[quote(remote_obj.pk)],
	current_app=self.model_admin.admin_site.name
)
However, I don't know if there are any side effects and I have not yet run the full suite of tests on this. Mostly looking for feedback whether I'm on the right track.

history.content:
Please solve this issue: Wrong URL generated by get_admin_url for readonly field in custom Admin Site
Description
	
When a model containing a ForeignKey field is viewed (or edited) in a custom Admin Site, and that ForeignKey field is listed in readonly_fields, the url generated for the link is /admin/... instead of /custom-admin/....
This appears to be caused by the following line in django.contrib.admin.helpers get_admin_url:
url = reverse(url_name, args=[quote(remote_obj.pk)])
Other parts of the admin use the current_app keyword parameter to identify the correct current name of the Admin Site. (See django.contrib.admin.options.ModelAdmin response_add as just one example)
I have been able to correct this specific issue by replacing the above line with:
url = reverse(
	url_name,
	args=[quote(remote_obj.pk)],
	current_app=self.model_admin.admin_site.name
)
However, I don't know if there are any side effects and I have not yet run the full suite of tests on this. Mostly looking for feedback whether I'm on the right track.

Please solve this issue: Wrong URL generated by get_admin_url for readonly field in custom Admin Site
Description
	
When a model containing a ForeignKey field is viewed (or edited) in a custom Admin Site, and that ForeignKey field is listed in readonly_fields, the url generated for the link is /admin/... instead of /custom-admin/....
This appears to be caused by the following line in django.contrib.admin.helpers get_admin_url:
url = reverse(url_name, args=[quote(remote_obj.pk)])
Other parts of the admin use the current_app keyword parameter to identify the correct current name of the Admin Site. (See django.contrib.admin.options.ModelAdmin response_add as just one example)
I have been able to correct this specific issue by replacing the above line with:
url = reverse(
	url_name,
	args=[quote(remote_obj.pk)],
	current_app=self.model_admin.admin_site.name
)
However, I don't know if there are any side effects and I have not yet run the full suite of tests on this. Mostly looking for feedback whether I'm on the right track.

Please solve this issue: Wrong URL generated by get_admin_url for readonly field in custom Admin Site
Description
	
When a model containing a ForeignKey field is viewed (or edited) in a custom Admin Site, and that ForeignKey field is listed in readonly_fields, the url generated for the link is /admin/... instead of /custom-admin/....
This appears to be caused by the following line in django.contrib.admin.helpers get_admin_url:
url = reverse(url_name, args=[quote(remote_obj.pk)])
Other parts of the admin use the current_app keyword parameter to identify the correct current name of the Admin Site. (See django.contrib.admin.options.ModelAdmin response_add as just one example)
I have been able to correct this specific issue by replacing the above line with:
url = reverse(
	url_name,
	args=[quote(remote_obj.pk)],
	current_app=self.model_admin.admin_site.name
)
However, I don't know if there are any side effects and I have not yet run the full suite of tests on this. Mostly looking for feedback whether I'm on the right track.

This appears to be caused by the following line in django.contrib.admin.helpers get_admin_url:
url = reverse(url_name, args=[quote(remote_obj.pk)])
Other parts of the admin use the current_app keyword parameter to identify the correct current name of the Admin Site. (See django.contrib.admin.options.ModelAdmin response_add as just one example)
I have been able to correct this specific issue by replacing the above line with:
url = reverse(
	url_name,
	args=[quote(remote_obj.pk)],
	current_app=self.model_admin.admin_site.name
)
However, I don't know if there are any side effects and I have not yet run the full suite of tests on this. Mostly looking for feedback whether I'm on the right track.

Description
	
When a model containing a ForeignKey field is viewed (or edited) in a custom Admin Site, and that ForeignKey field is listed in readonly_fields, the url generated for the link is /admin/... instead of /custom-admin/....
This appears to be caused by the following line in django.contrib.admin.helpers get_admin_url:
url = reverse(url_name, args=[quote(remote_obj.pk)])
Other parts of the admin use the current_app keyword parameter to identify the correct current name of the Admin Site. (See django.contrib.admin.options.ModelAdmin response_add as just one example)
I have been able to correct this specific issue by replacing the above line with:
url = reverse(
	url_name,
	args=[quote(remote_obj.pk)],
	current_app=self.model_admin.admin_site.name
)
However, I don't know if there are any side effects and I have not yet run the full suite of tests on this. Mostly looking for feedback whether I'm on the right track.

Please solve this issue: Wrong URL generated by get_admin_url for readonly field in custom Admin Site
Description
	
When a model containing a ForeignKey field is viewed (or edited) in a custom Admin Site, and that ForeignKey field is listed in readonly_fields, the url generated for the link is /admin/... instead of /custom-admin/....
This appears to be caused by the following line in django.contrib.admin.helpers get_admin_url:
url = reverse(url_name, args=[quote(remote_obj.pk)])
Other parts of the admin use the current_app keyword parameter to identify the correct current name of the Admin Site. (See django.contrib.admin.options.ModelAdmin response_add as just one example)
I have been able to correct this specific issue by replacing the above line with:
url = reverse(
	url_name,
	args=[quote(remote_obj.pk)],
	current_app=self.model_admin.admin_site.name
)
However, I don't know if there are any side effects and I have not yet run the full suite of tests on this. Mostly looking for feedback whether I'm on the right track.

Please solve this issue: Wrong URL generated by get_admin_url for readonly field in custom Admin Site
Description
	
When a model containing a ForeignKey field is viewed (or edited) in a custom Admin Site, and that ForeignKey field is listed in readonly_fields, the url generated for the link is /admin/... instead of /custom-admin/....
This appears to be caused by the following line in django.contrib.admin.helpers get_admin_url:
url = reverse(url_name, args=[quote(remote_obj.pk)])
Other parts of the admin use the current_app keyword parameter to identify the correct current name of the Admin Site. (See django.contrib.admin.options.ModelAdmin response_add as just one example)
I have been able to correct this specific issue by replacing the above line with:
url = reverse(
	url_name,
	args=[quote(remote_obj.pk)],
	current_app=self.model_admin.admin_site.name
)
However, I don't know if there are any side effects and I have not yet run the full suite of tests on this. Mostly looking for feedback whether I'm on the right track.

Please solve this issue: Wrong URL generated by get_admin_url for readonly field in custom Admin Site
Description
	
When a model containing a ForeignKey field is viewed (or edited) in a custom Admin Site, and that ForeignKey field is listed in readonly_fields, the url generated for the link is /admin/... instead of /custom-admin/....
This appears to be caused by the following line in django.contrib.admin.helpers get_admin_url:
url = reverse(url_name, args=[quote(remote_obj.pk)])
Other parts of the admin use the current_app keyword parameter to identify the correct current name of the Admin Site. (See django.contrib.admin.options.ModelAdmin response_add as just one example)
I have been able to correct this specific issue by replacing the above line with:
url = reverse(
	url_name,
	args=[quote(remote_obj.pk)],
	current_app=self.model_admin.admin_site.name
)
However, I don't know if there are any side effects and I have not yet run the full suite of tests on this. Mostly looking for feedback whether I'm on the right track.

history.content:
Please solve this issue: Wrong URL generated by get_admin_url for readonly field in custom Admin Site
Description
	
When a model containing a ForeignKey field is viewed (or edited) in a custom Admin Site, and that ForeignKey field is listed in readonly_fields, the url generated for the link is /admin/... instead of /custom-admin/....
This appears to be caused by the following line in django.contrib.admin.helpers get_admin_url:
url = reverse(url_name, args=[quote(remote_obj.pk)])
Other parts of the admin use the current_app keyword parameter to identify the correct current name of the Admin Site. (See django.contrib.admin.options.ModelAdmin response_add as just one example)
I have been able to correct this specific issue by replacing the above line with:
url = reverse(
	url_name,
	args=[quote(remote_obj.pk)],
	current_app=self.model_admin.admin_site.name
)
However, I don't know if there are any side effects and I have not yet run the full suite of tests on this. Mostly looking for feedback whether I'm on the right track.

Please solve this issue: Wrong URL generated by get_admin_url for readonly field in custom Admin Site
Description
	
When a model containing a ForeignKey field is viewed (or edited) in a custom Admin Site, and that ForeignKey field is listed in readonly_fields, the url generated for the link is /admin/... instead of /custom-admin/....
This appears to be caused by the following line in django.contrib.admin.helpers get_admin_url:
url = reverse(url_name, args=[quote(remote_obj.pk)])
Other parts of the admin use the current_app keyword parameter to identify the correct current name of the Admin Site. (See django.contrib.admin.options.ModelAdmin response_add as just one example)
I have been able to correct this specific issue by replacing the above line with:
url = reverse(
	url_name,
	args=[quote(remote_obj.pk)],
	current_app=self.model_admin.admin_site.name
)
However, I don't know if there are any side effects and I have not yet run the full suite of tests on this. Mostly looking for feedback whether I'm on the right track.

Please solve this issue: Wrong URL generated by get_admin_url for readonly field in custom Admin Site
Description
	
When a model containing a ForeignKey field is viewed (or edited) in a custom Admin Site, and that ForeignKey field is listed in readonly_fields, the url generated for the link is /admin/... instead of /custom-admin/....
This appears to be caused by the following line in django.contrib.admin.helpers get_admin_url:
url = reverse(url_name, args=[quote(remote_obj.pk)])
Other parts of the admin use the current_app keyword parameter to identify the correct current name of the Admin Site. (See django.contrib.admin.options.ModelAdmin response_add as just one example)
I have been able to correct this specific issue by replacing the above line with:
url = reverse(
	url_name,
	args=[quote(remote_obj.pk)],
	current_app=self.model_admin.admin_site.name
)
However, I don't know if there are any side effects and I have not yet run the full suite of tests on this. Mostly looking for feedback whether I'm on the right track.

Please solve this issue: Wrong URL generated by get_admin_url for readonly field in custom Admin Site
Description
	
When a model containing a ForeignKey field is viewed (or edited) in a custom Admin Site, and that ForeignKey field is listed in readonly_fields, the url generated for the link is /admin/... instead of /custom-admin/....
This appears to be caused by the following line in django.contrib.admin.helpers get_admin_url:
url = reverse(url_name, args=[quote(remote_obj.pk)])
Other parts of the admin use the current_app keyword parameter to identify the correct current name of the Admin Site. (See django.contrib.admin.options.ModelAdmin response_add as just one example)
I have been able to correct this specific issue by replacing the above line with:
url = reverse(
	url_name,
	args=[quote(remote_obj.pk)],
	current_app=self.model_admin.admin_site.name
)
However, I don't know if there are any side effects and I have not yet run the full suite of tests on this. Mostly looking for feedback whether I'm on the right track.

Please solve this issue: Wrong URL generated by get_admin_url for readonly field in custom Admin Site
Description
	
When a model containing a ForeignKey field is viewed (or edited) in a custom Admin Site, and that ForeignKey field is listed in readonly_fields, the url generated for the link is /admin/... instead of /custom-admin/....
This appears to be caused by the following line in django.contrib.admin.helpers get_admin_url:
url = reverse(url_name, args=[quote(remote_obj.pk)])
Other parts of the admin use the current_app keyword parameter to identify the correct current name of the Admin Site. (See django.contrib.admin.options.ModelAdmin response_add as just one example)
I have been able to correct this specific issue by replacing the above line with:
url = reverse(
	url_name,
	args=[quote(remote_obj.pk)],
	current_app=self.model_admin.admin_site.name
)
However, I don't know if there are any side effects and I have not yet run the full suite of tests on this. Mostly looking for feedback whether I'm on the right track.

        article = Article.objects.create(

            date=datetime.datetime(2021, 1, 1), section=section,

        # admin_views.Section is not registered on the default admin site, so

Please solve this issue: Wrong URL generated by get_admin_url for readonly field in custom Admin Site
Description
	
When a model containing a ForeignKey field is viewed (or edited) in a custom Admin Site, and that ForeignKey field is listed in readonly_fields, the url generated for the link is /admin/... instead of /custom-admin/....
This appears to be caused by the following line in django.contrib.admin.helpers get_admin_url:
url = reverse(url_name, args=[quote(remote_obj.pk)])
Other parts of the admin use the current_app keyword parameter to identify the correct current name of the Admin Site. (See django.contrib.admin.options.ModelAdmin response_add as just one example)
I have been able to correct this specific issue by replacing the above line with:
url = reverse(
	url_name,
	args=[quote(remote_obj.pk)],
	current_app=self.model_admin.admin_site.name
)
However, I don't know if there are any side effects and I have not yet run the full suite of tests on this. Mostly looking for feedback whether I'm on the right track.

class ReadonlyForeignKeyCustomAdminSiteTests(TestCase):
    def _make_field(self, admin_site):
        section = Section.objects.create(name='section')
        article = Article.objects.create(
            title='article', content='content',
            date=datetime.datetime(2021, 1, 1), section=section,
        )
        from django.contrib.admin import ModelAdmin

        model_admin = ArticleAdmin(Article, admin_site)

        field = AdminReadonlyField(form, 'section', False, model_admin=model_admin)

        field, section = self._make_field(custom_site)
        remote_field = Article._meta.get_field('section').remote_field
        url = field.get_admin_url(remote_field, section)
        expected = reverse(
            'admin2:admin_views_section_change',
            args=[section.pk],
            current_app=custom_site.name,
        )
        self.assertIn('href="%s"' % expected, str(url))
        self.assertIn('/test_admin/admin2/', str(url))

        from django.contrib import admin as contrib_admin
        field, section = self._make_field(contrib_admin.site)
        remote_field = Article._meta.get_field('section').remote_field
        # admin_views.Section is not registered on the default admin site, so
        # NoReverseMatch is handled gracefully by falling back to str().
        self.assertEqual(field.get_admin_url(remote_field, section), str(section))
